h1: The 6 Best Printer Cabinets for Home Offices of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six printer cabinets for home offices, compared on drawers, locks, casters and top space to find the right fit.
summary: The DEVAISE 3-drawer cabinet is the best printer cabinet for most home offices: roomy, mobile and flat on top. The Letaya 3-drawer adds locks and a metal build. The VASAGLE CUSTOS is the compact choice, while the Letaya 2-drawer lateral gives wide laser printers the biggest deck.
intro: Printer cabinets are sold on their drawers and judged on their tops. The drawers are what show up in lifestyle photos, but the printer lives on the deck, and a deck even an inch too small leaves a foot hanging in the air. Every jam, every pulled paper tray and every bumped cable then tests whether the cabinet is stable.

We reviewed eight cabinets and ranked six on spec sheets: drawer count, locks, casters, build material and the size of the open top. Each pick has a flat surface meant to hold a printer, and each is placed by how well it balances storage, mobility and footprint. Measure your printer's width and depth before reading further, because that number settles half of these choices.

products.name: DEVAISE 3-Drawer Mobile File Cabinet
products.verdict: Three lateral drawers, casters, and a flat top make it the easiest all-round printer perch.
products.description:
The DEVAISE is a three-drawer mobile file cabinet in a rustic brown finish, with lateral open drawers, a rolling caster base and a flat, open top. Lateral drawers pull wide and hold files side to side, which suits a stack of paper, ink and cables better than a narrow vertical stack. Casters let you roll it out to clear a jam.

It ranks first because it balances storage, mobility and a deck that fits most printers at a modest price. The Letaya below adds locks and metal, but looks more like office furniture, and the VASAGLE has one fewer drawer.

Buy it for paper and supply storage under an inkjet or all-in-one. The caveat is that no drawer lock is listed and it is not metal, so skip it for sensitive files or a heavy laser printer.
products.idealFor: A home office that needs mobile paper and supply storage under a printer.
products.skipIf: You need lockable storage for sensitive files.

products.name: Letaya 3 Drawer Mobile File Cabinet with Lock
products.verdict: Fully assembled metal cabinet with three lockable drawers and a flat printer deck.
products.description:
The Letaya 3-drawer cabinet has lockable drawers, a metal build, an open flat top, and arrives fully assembled. Cheap metal locks deter casual snooping rather than a determined thief, but in a shared house they keep tax records and client files out of casual view. Hanging support covers letter, legal and A4 documents.

It ranks second because the DEVAISE gives the same drawer count with a softer look and no lock. Compared with the Letaya 2-drawer lateral below, this one rolls on casters and holds more files, though its deck is less wide.

Buy it for private paperwork under a printer. The caveat is the plain office look and the extra weight: metal and casters make it heavier to move, and it will not blend into a living room.
products.idealFor: Anyone storing client or personal paperwork who wants a lock.
products.skipIf: Your room needs a softer, furniture-style look.

products.name: VASAGLE CUSTOS Collection 2-Drawer File Cabinet, Printer Stand
products.verdict: A small, rolling two-drawer cabinet at about 15.7 by 16.5 by 27.6 inches.
products.description:
The VASAGLE CUSTOS Collection is a two-drawer cabinet at 15.7 x 16.5 x 27.6 inches, fitting letter or A4 files, with rolling casters and a matte black finish. It is marketed explicitly as a printer stand and file cabinet, which means the top is designed for the job and the footprint is among the smallest here.

It sits third because two drawers hold far less than the DEVAISE's three, and the small top limits you to compact printers. It does fit under a desk and in corners that a lateral cabinet would block.

Buy it for a tight desk setup where floor space is scarce and you file lightly. Skip it if you handle paper every month, since two drawers fill quickly, and check your printer's footprint against the 15.7 by 16.5 inch deck first.
products.idealFor: Small desks and tight corners where floor space is scarce.
products.skipIf: You file a lot of paper every month.

products.name: Letaya 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Metal Lateral Filing Cabinet
products.verdict: A wide 28-inch lateral metal cabinet with two lockable drawers.
products.description:
The Letaya 2-drawer lateral cabinet is metal, with two lockable lateral drawers, a deck about 28 inches wide, and hanging support for letter, legal and A4 files. Its measured size is 27.95 x 28.35 x 15.74 inches. A wide, shallow deck gives a large laser or all-in-one printer room on every side, which narrow cabinets cannot.

It ranks fourth because it has no casters listed, which makes it a fixed station, and it takes up wall length. The DEVAISE and Letaya 3-drawer both roll.

Buy it for a printer that stays put, with locked storage below. Skip it if you need to move the cabinet between rooms. Check the 15.74 inch depth against your printer, since a deep machine may not sit entirely on the deck.
products.idealFor: A fixed printer station with locked storage underneath.
products.skipIf: You need to move the cabinet between rooms.

products.name: GYIIYUO 2 Drawer File Cabinet with 24-Inch Extended Desktop
products.verdict: A 24-inch extended desktop adds workspace beside the printer.
products.description:
The GYIIYUO two-drawer cabinet adds a 24 inch extended desktop, rolling casters, fabric drawer fronts and a side storage bag. The extension turns it into a small workstation: the printer sits on the main deck and a laptop or papers sit on the overhang.

It ranks fifth because the overhang limits how much you can safely put on the extension, and no lock is listed. Its fabric fronts give it a softer, apartment-friendly look that the metal Letaya models lack.

Buy it for a small apartment where one piece must do two jobs. The caveat is load: keep heavy gear off the extended section, and place the printer over the supported cabinet body, not over the overhang.
products.idealFor: Small apartments that need one piece doing two jobs.
products.skipIf: You plan to put heavy gear on the extension.

products.name: SISESOL 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Narrow Vertical Filing Cabinet
products.verdict: A narrow metal vertical cabinet with two lockable drawers at the lowest price tier here.
products.description:
The SISESOL is a narrow vertical metal cabinet with two lockable drawers and an open flat top, at the lowest price tier here. Vertical drawers stack narrow and deep, which saves floor width. The lock and metal build are rare at this price.

It ranks last because the small top surface cannot take a wide laser or all-in-one, and no casters are listed. The Letaya 2-drawer carries a bigger printer for a modest premium.

Buy it for a compact inkjet on a budget, tucked into a corner. Skip it if you own a wide printer, since the narrow deck would leave its feet hanging over the edge. Measure the footprint before you order.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers with a compact inkjet.
products.skipIf: You own a wide laser or all-in-one printer.

whatMatters.detail: The top is the printer's platform, and it must exceed the printer's footprint on every side. A deck that is too small lets feet hang over and invites tipping when you pull a tray. Measure your printer's width and depth, then compare them to the cabinet's listed dimensions before ordering, and leave a margin of an inch or so.

Lateral drawers pull out wide and hold files side to side, while vertical drawers stack narrow and deep. Lateral models suit wider printers, and vertical ones fit tight corners. Check whether the listing says letter, legal or A4 files fit, and whether hanging file rails are included or sold separately.

A lock keeps client files or tax records private in a shared home. Cheap cabinet locks deter casual access, not theft. Look for the word lockable in the product title or bullets, confirm that keys are included, and treat a lock as privacy, not security. The DEVAISE and VASAGLE do not list locks, while the Letaya models and SISESOL do.

Rolling wheels let you pull the cabinet out to clear paper jams or reach the power cord. They also mean the cabinet can shift if bumped. Check the listing for locking casters, especially if your floor is uneven. Fixed cabinets like the Letaya 2-drawer stay put, which some people prefer for a heavy printer that rarely moves.

Metal cabinets handle more weight and often include locks, while wood-look boards blend into a living space. Heavier printers do better on metal. Confirm the material in the title or bullet points, not just the photo, and note how much weight the top is meant to carry before placing a laser printer on it.

faq.q: Will my printer fit on these cabinets?
faq.a: Each has an open flat top, but sizes vary. Compare your printer's width and depth to the cabinet's listed dimensions, and leave a margin so the feet sit fully on the surface. The Letaya 2-drawer has the widest deck.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Buying for drawers and ignoring the top. A printer overhanging its deck is unstable and can tip when you pull a tray. Measure the printer first, then pick between the DEVAISE and the VASAGLE based on space.

faq.q: Is a lockable cabinet worth it over an unlocked one?
faq.a: Only if you store sensitive papers such as tax or client files. The Letaya and SISESOL picks have locks. For paper and ink supplies, an unlocked model like the DEVAISE is fine and keeps the price lower.

faq.q: Do I need to assemble these?
faq.a: The Letaya 3-drawer is listed as fully assembled, so it is ready to use. Others may need setup, so check the listing and the included hardware before ordering. The SISESOL lists easy assembly.

faq.q: How do I keep a rolling cabinet from shifting?
faq.a: Place it on a flat, level floor and check whether the casters lock before you load the top. Park it against a wall or desk leg when the printer runs, since printing vibration plus a bumped cord can make a rolling cabinet drift.

faq.q: Can a narrow cabinet hold a laser printer?
faq.a: Often not. Laser printers are wider and heavier, so a wide metal option like the Letaya 2-drawer is safer than the narrow SISESOL. Check the deck depth and the manufacturer's weight guidance on the listing.

finalTake: The DEVAISE 3-drawer is the right printer cabinet for most home offices because it rolls, stores plenty and gives a printer a proper deck. Choose the Letaya 3-drawer when files need a lock, the VASAGLE CUSTOS for tight spaces, and the Letaya lateral for wide printers. Measure the printer's footprint first, since the top decides everything.
